Quick answers

The things people ask most often before they dig into the guides below.

Do I have to install anything, or does my image get uploaded somewhere?

Neither. The Cropper is a single web page that runs entirely in your browser. Your image is read, measured, cropped and zipped locally - it never leaves your machine, and there's no account, server or upload involved.

Why does my artwork look shrunk or blurry after I upload it to Steam?

Steam checks the stored dimensions of an image when it displays it and quietly downscales anything it thinks is oversized. Every file this tool exports is already hexified (its last byte rewritten) so that check reads a smaller size and leaves the image alone. If it still looks shrunk, you most likely uploaded an un-hexified copy, or skipped the console step in the upload guide.

Does it work with animated GIFs?

Yes - Artwork, Workshop and Background all accept animated GIFs. Frames are cropped individually and re-encoded. If a GIF comes out over Steam's 5 MB limit, the tool drops frames (keeping the overall playback length) until it fits, or tells you it couldn't.

Is the console command safe? Can it get my account banned?

The command only changes a few hidden fields in Steam's own image-upload form before you save - it doesn't touch any game, the Steam client, or VAC. It's a profile-customization technique the community has used for years and it's what every tool of this kind relies on. That said, it isn't an officially supported feature, so use it at your own discretion.

What's the difference between "Artwork Creator" and "Background Cropper"?

Two modes of the same tool. Artwork Creator handles the Featured, Artwork and Workshop showcases and lets you add text/border layers. Background Cropper handles the full-page profile background and previews it with the real avatar and showcases sitting on top. See Creating your artwork.

Is this affiliated with Valve or Steam?

No. It's an independent tool. Steam and the Steam logo are trademarks of Valve Corporation; all other trademarks are property of their respective owners.

Reference

How Steam showcases work

Steam has no upload button for an Artwork Showcase, a Workshop panorama or a profile background. Each one is an image slipped in through an unrelated editor, and none of them render at full size until the file is tampered with. This is the geometry each crop has to hit - the model the Cropper is built against.

Two Steam-side quirks shape everything the tool does. 1 - the console command: Artwork, Screenshot and Workshop images all pass through Steam's Guide image editor, which never asks which showcase you mean, so a one-line command answers that before you save. 2 - hexify: Steam downscales images it judges oversized at display time, so the file's last non-zero byte is rewritten to 0x21 - which changes what Steam's size check reads without touching any byte a decoder needs. The step-by-step for both is in Uploading to Steam.

Artwork & Screenshot Showcase

The Artwork Showcase sits in the profile's 652px left column, inside a block with ~10px padding each side - about 632px of usable width. One artwork is a single image. With two, it splits into a primary panel rendered 506px wide beside a secondary column 100px wide, ~9px gutter between. With three or more, the secondary column stacks a shorter image on a 57px "+N more" counter, and the two columns are forced to equal total height.

The panorama trick: take one tall image, cut a 506-wide slice from the left and a 100-wide slice from the right edge - both from the same rows - and upload them as artwork #1 and #2. On the profile they read as one uncut picture. The catch: the slices render at different widths, so for their heights to match, the right slice's source width has to be leftSliceWidth × 100 / 506, not simply 100px. Solving that split is the whole job of an artwork cropper. The Screenshot Showcase is the identical layout - only file_type = 5 at upload differs.

Workshop Showcase

The Workshop Showcase shows up to five Workshop submissions in a strip inside that same ~632px block. Steam's CSS gives each item a fifth of the block minus its 2px margins, so a slot is 122.4px wide with ~4px between slots - the reconstructed panorama runs slot 1's left edge to slot 5's right edge, about 628px. Upload one wide image cut into five consecutive vertical slices as five items - against consumer_app_id = 480, Steam's test app, so it needn't be a real submission - and the strip reads as one panorama. Slice height is whatever the tallest slice is.

Profile Background & Featured Showcase

The profile background is a full-bleed image behind the whole profile. Steam centers it horizontally and shows it up to 1920px wide; only an ultra-wide window stretches it past that. Nothing is cropped to an aspect ratio - a 2560×1440 source just shows its middle 1920px. Points Shop backgrounds are 1920×1080; Market ones vary; a 512×512 one tiles. Animated backgrounds are .webm served from Steam's CDN with a .jpg poster.

Because the background sits under everything, the advanced move - what steam.design automates - is cropping the background itself into the regions behind the avatar and the artwork showcase so the profile looks like one continuous composition. The Background Cropper's “Slice for showcases” mode does this: it cuts the exact rectangle each showcase covers (Artwork primary 506 + side 100, Featured 630, Avatar 164) so the piece reads as an uncut continuation of the background. The Featured Showcase is the simple case: 630px wide, any height, one continuous image sharing the artwork region's left edge.

The spec sheet

Rendered widths - the size an image actually occupies on the profile, which is what a crop targets. Sources: steam.design's published crop configuration and Steam's profilev2.css.

ElementRendered sizeNotes
Profile left column652 px~632px usable inside the customization block
Artwork - primary506 × hthe wide panel; height is free
Artwork - secondary100 × hrenders ~9px right of the primary
Artwork - "+N" box100 × 57appears with 3+ artworks, 11px below the secondary image
Featured Showcase630 × hsingle continuous image
Workshop slot~122.4 × h5 across a ~628px strip, ~4px gaps
Avatar (in-composition)164 × 164region behind the header avatar; upload source is 184²
Background - display width≤ 1920 pxcentered; wider only on ultra-wide windows

How the Cropper maps to this

Artwork split Match

Targets the 506 / 100 rendered widths and solves for the source split that makes both slices the same on-page height. The "+N" box is handled by the "Bottom right space" toggle.

Featured Showcase Match

Fixed 630px width, height scaled from the source. Exactly the spec.

Workshop slicing Match

Slots are 122.4px wide; a source maps onto the 5 × 122.4 + 4 × 4 = 628px strip between slot 1 and slot 5, with the ~4px gaps discarded.

Profile background Match

A static background keeps its native resolution (Steam shows it native, centered - it isn't scaled to fit); only an animated background is scaled to 1920px wide, the way Steam pins it. Forces no aspect ratio.

Hexify Match

Every exported image is hexified before zipping so Steam renders it at full size - a per-format nudge for JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP.

Background → region compositing Partial

The Background Cropper's "Slice for showcases" mode cuts one background into Artwork (506 + 100), Screenshot (506 + 100), Featured (630), single Workshop (160) and Avatar (164) pieces, stacked in your profile's showcase order. Workshop grids, Guide showcases and animated-background slicing are still to come.

Guide

How to create Steam artwork

The Cropper measures and cuts all four profile-image types for you, in the browser, with nothing uploaded anywhere. Here's the whole flow.

1

Load your image. Click Select image and pick a file, paste a direct image link in the URL box and hit Load, or drag an image anywhere onto the page. Static images (PNG/JPG) and animated GIFs both work.

2

Pick what you're making. Two modes sit in the top bar. Artwork Creator covers the Featured, Artwork and Workshop showcases - switch between them with the format buttons, and the preview redraws inside a pixel-accurate mock of the Steam profile. Background Cropper covers the profile background and applies your image as the page background so you can see how the avatar and showcases sit on top of it.

3

Adjust for the format.

  • Featured - nothing to set; any height works, it's scaled to 630px wide.
  • Artwork - the tool solves the wide/narrow split for you. Tick Bottom right space if your profile shows 3 or more artworks (it leaves room for the "+N more" counter). GIF-only: Fix gif trail, Disable gif transparency.
  • Workshop - Disable slider is on by default and cuts the whole image into 5 slices. Uncheck it to drag a slider and pick one horizontal band instead. If the source is smaller than the strip, tick Resize image to fit whole showcase.
  • Background - native resolution is kept; it's only scaled down if it's wider than 1920px.
4

Add text or borders (optional). In Artwork Creator, + Text and + Border add overlay layers that are baked into every exported image and hexified along with it. Select a layer in the list to edit its properties.

5

Export. Hit Export to download a zip of the finished images. Each one is already hexified so Steam shows it at full size, and oversized files are auto-compressed under Steam's 5 MB limit (oversized GIFs drop frames, keeping total duration, until they fit). Then follow Uploading to Steam below.

Tips
  • Keep your browser window maximized while you work - the preview mirrors the real Steam profile layout.
  • Nothing leaves your machine; the Cropper is entirely client-side.
  • Every zip includes a readme.txt with the upload steps, so you have them offline.
  • Not sure what size anything should be? See How Steam showcases work.

Uploading to Steam

Cropping is only half the job - Steam has no normal upload button for these showcase types. Here's exactly how to get each one live, with copy-paste steps for every case.

Why the console command? Artwork, Screenshot and Workshop Showcase images all go through Steam's Guide image editor, which normally expects a guide's cover image - not a showcase piece. The one-line command below tells that editor which showcase type and dimensions you actually mean before you save, which is the same trick the wider Steam customization community has used for years.

Artwork Showcase

The wide/thin image pair the Cropper's Artwork tab produces.

1

Open steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/edititem/767/3/

2

Select your artwork image.

3

Right-click anywhere on the page → Inspect → open the Console tab.

4

Paste this and press Enter:

$J('#image_width').val(1000),$J('#image_height').val(1);
5

Click Save and Continue, then set your profile's Artwork Showcase to display it.

Screenshot Showcase

Same flow as Artwork Showcase, with one extra field set.

1

Open steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/edititem/767/3/

2

Select your artwork image.

3

Right-click anywhere on the page → Inspect → open the Console tab.

4

Paste this and press Enter:

$J('#image_width').val(1000),$J('#image_height').val(1),$J('[name=file_type]').val(5);
5

Click Save and Continue.

Workshop Showcase

The 5-slice strip the Cropper's Workshop tab produces - upload all five images this way.

1

Open steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/edititem/767/3/

2

Select one slice.

3

Right-click anywhere on the page → Inspect → open the Console tab.

4

Paste this and press Enter:

$J('[name=consumer_app_id]').val(480),$J('[name=file_type]').val(0),$J('[name=visibility]').val(0);
5

Click Save and Continue. Repeat for the other four slices, then order them 1–5 in your Workshop Showcase.

Guide Showcase

Not something this Cropper exports, but the same trick applies - included for the full picture.

1

Open the editor for the icon style you want:

Steam Icon → Transparent Icon →
2

Select your artwork image.

3

Click Save and Continue - no console step needed for either icon style.

Long Guide

For a tall Guide Showcase image instead of a small icon.

1

Open steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/edititem/767/3/

2

Select your artwork image.

3

Right-click anywhere on the page → Inspect → open the Console tab.

4

Paste this and press Enter:

$J('[name=consumer_app_id]').val(753);$J('#image_width').val('1000');$J('#image_height').val('1');$J('[name=file_type]').val('9');
5

Click Save and Continue.
